title: Risk Factors for Injuries in Runners: A Systematic Review of Foot Strike Technique and Its Classification at Impact
claims: The review included 13 studies exploring the relationship between foot strike technique and running-related injuries.
Six studies reported foot strike categorically and seven reported continuous measures such as foot contact angle, ankle flexion angle and strike index.

Three of the six categorical studies found rearfoot strikers had a significantly greater retrospective injury rate than non-rearfoot strikers, while one other study reported greater risk with midfoot and forefoot striking.
Only one of the seven studies using continuous measures reported a significant relationship with running-related injuries.

The GRADE table rated foot strike pattern evidence as very low; the structured abstract calls it low. The review notes retrospective designs, small samples and poor foot strike assessment, and calls for larger prospective studies.
